title: Review F — Edge, WAF, DDoS & anti-automation
description:
> ## ✅ F-9 RESOLVED — added 2026-08-17. **The row is FALSE at the live edge: all three portals already serve their own CSP. Do NOT add one at the gateway — it would break them.**
>
> **F-9 is closed on this ticket. KS-491 itself stays OPEN** for the two rows that are still live: the **strategic WAF gap** and the **absent Caddyfile**.
>
> ### 1. The claim, tested at the internet-facing edge
>
> Three read-only GETs against `https://secuura02-demo.southeastasia.cloudapp.azure.com`:
>
> | Path | CSP served? | Distinguishing directive |
> | -- | -- | -- |
> | `/` (issuer) | **yes** | `script-src … 'unsafe-eval'` — issuer only |
> | `/admin/` | **yes** | `connect-src … wss://*.secuura.io` — admin only |
> | `/verify/` | **yes** | `frame-ancestors 'self' https://*.secuura.io https://secuura.io` |
>
> **They differ from one another, and that difference is the discriminator.** A single `add_header` at the gateway would make all three byte-identical. Control: `/api/health` returns a **fourth, different** CSP from the API service — so a CSP on this host is not a gateway-wide artefact.
>
> Source side agrees: **8** `Content-Security-Policy` occurrences across `frontend/{issuer,verifier,admin,outlook-addin}/nginx.conf`, and the gateway does **not** `proxy_hide_header Content-Security-Policy`, so downstream policies pass through untouched. It *does* hide-and-re-add `X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy` and HSTS — which is why those five are gateway-owned and CSP is not. The file is internally consistent.
>
> ### 2. The gateway's abstention is a decision, and it is NEWER than this row
>
> `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf:240-245`, immediately above the live header block:
>
> > *"CSP is DELIBERATELY NOT SET HERE. It is app-specific — issuer, admin and verifier each ship their own — and a single generic policy at the gateway would either be too loose to be worth having or would break a portal. Owning it here would also silently override a tighter downstream policy. That stays with the apps; tracked as its own decision, not smuggled in."*
>
> `git log -S"DELIBERATELY NOT SET HERE"` attributes it to exactly one commit — `045c658ec`**, 2026-08-13, "KS-613/KS-615: harden the live gateway edge…" (#678)** — the same hardening pass that fixed F-2, F-6 and F-7. Sentinel control returns empty. **The missing gateway CSP is not an oversight this review caught; it is a decision the F-remediation took afterwards, in writing.**
>
> ### 3. Why "just add one" is actively harmful, not merely redundant
>
> Two `Content-Security-Policy` headers are **not merged**. Each policy is enforced independently, so a resource must satisfy **both** — the effective policy is the **intersection**. Intersecting the commented-out `:595` policy against what admin actually serves:
>
> | directive | `:595` policy | admin's live policy | effective | consequence |
> | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
> | `connect-src` | `'self' https://*.blockfrost.io` | `'self' http://localhost:* https://*.secuura.io wss://*.secuura.io` | `'self'` | **admin's XHR/WebSocket blocked** |
> | `script-src` | `'self' 'unsafe-inline'` | `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` | `'self'` | **wasm blocked, all three portals** |
> | `img-src` | `'self' data: https:` | `'self' data: https: blob:` | loses `blob:` | **blob images blocked** |
> | `worker-src` | absent → falls back to `script-src` | `'self' blob:` | loses `blob:` | **blob workers blocked** |
>
> That is the portal-breaking outcome the in-file comment predicts, arrived at independently.
>
> ### 4. Recorded so it is not re-derived
>
> Two things stated explicitly because a later reader will otherwise repeat the work:
>
> * `frame-ancestors` **is NOT part of the breakage.** It does not fall back to `default-src`, so an unspecified `frame-ancestors` in a gateway policy leaves each portal's own value governing. An earlier note of mine claimed otherwise; it was wrong and the four rows above stand without it.
> * `outlook-addin` **is not routed through this gateway** (0 matches for `outlook` in `nginx-demo.conf`), so its policy is unaffected either way.
>
> ### 5. The real question this surfaced → **KS-648**
>
> The policies exist and are well-formed, but two directives are weak: `'unsafe-eval'` **on the issuer alone** (the other two manage on `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`) and `'unsafe-inline'` **styles on all three**. That is an app-level quality question, exactly as the in-file comment says — filed as [KS-648](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-648), Low, in the Security Review project. **Not** part of F-9.
>
> *Established read-only: three GETs,* `git log -S`*, and greps over the tree. No code changed, nothing deployed, no probe whose success path writes. F-9's deploy authorisation was retired rather than released.*

---

> ## ⚠️ STATUS BANNER — added 2026-08-16. **The table below says "0** `limit_req`**, 0** `client_max_body_size`**". That is now FALSE, and the fix is CONFIRMED LIVE ON THE VM.**
>
> **This resolves the open question of whether F's edge hardening was merged-but-undeployed. It is deployed.** Established read-only, with no rate-limit or body-cap probe against the live demo.
>
> ### F-2 / F-7 — fixed in code **and live**
>
> | Measure | Register says | Repo today | **Running container** |
> | -- | -- | -- | -- |
> | `limit_req` | **0** | **9** | **9** |
> | `limit_conn` | 0 | **4** | — |
> | `client_max_body_size` | **0** | **12m** (`:215`) | — |
>
> **The proof that it is live, rather than merely merged:**
>
> * `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf` on the VM is **byte-identical to the repo copy** — md5 `8be17f5b075d51a170269cd404dc6a87` on both.
> * The **running** `secuura-nginx-gateway` **container** serves `/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf` at the **same md5**, so this is the config nginx actually loaded, not just a file sitting on the host disk.
> * Ordering closes it: conf mtime `2026-08-13T00:09:07Z`, container start `2026-08-14T05:06:57Z` — **the container started after the file's last modification**, so it cannot be serving an older copy. `nginx -t` passes.
>
> This matters because **the conf is bind-mounted, not baked into the image** — an image rebuild proves nothing about it either way, which is exactly why the merge alone was not evidence. Shipped by KS-613/#678 and KS-616/#679.
>
> ### Why the earlier "unestablished" reading was right at the time
>
> A single GET returns HSTS, CSP and `X-Frame-Options`, and **none of those discriminate**: the CSP cannot come from this conf (its own is commented out — see below), and Caddy terminates TLS in front, making HSTS unattributable. **Reading the mounted file was the check that discriminates**; the header response was not.
>
> ### Still open
>
> * **F-9 partial — CSP is still commented out at** `nginx-demo.conf:595`**.** `X-Frame-Options` and HSTS are active; the CSP line is inert. Verified today.
> * The **strategic Crit row (no WAF anywhere)** stands unchanged — it is a greenfield gap, not a stale row.
> * **Caddyfile still absent from the repo**, so the TLS edge remains unversioned.
>
> *Banner added during the session-38 closure sweep. Ticket left **open** for F-9's CSP, the WAF row, and the Caddyfile.*

Work-stream **F** of the [Platform K security review](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-485>). Forward-looking edge & resilience posture for a millions-of-users, continuously-attacked target. Largely a **gap analysis** — what's ABSENT matters as much as what's present. Recon complete on `develop` @ `fcf2d878c`.

**Scope / checklist**

* WAF: is any WAF present (nginx ModSecurity / Front Door / App Gateway WAF / Cloudflare)? Where would it integrate? (Product owner explicitly wants WAF.)
* Edge config: nginx gateway + Caddy — security headers, request-size limits, timeouts, TLS.
* Rate limiting / DDoS: edge + app tier; connection/request caps; Slowloris/large-body.
* Bot / anti-automation: CAPTCHA on signup/login/verify.
* Secret manager (runtime) & observability/alerting; network segmentation of infra services.

## Findings / recommendations (develop @ fcf2d878c)

| Sev | Evidence | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Crit (strategic) | repo-wide absent; `deployment/DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md:50` | **No WAF** anywhere — no ModSecurity, no Front Door/App Gateway WAF; Cloudflare is DNS-only (grey-cloud), so no Cloudflare WAF. Greenfield. Integration point: in front of Caddy (Front Door WAF) or a ModSecurity sidecar at the gateway. |
| High | `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf` (0 `limit_req`, 0 `client_max_body_size`) | The **live** gateway conf has no edge rate-limit and no request-body cap. The hardened `nginx-production.conf:21-22,216` (10r/s, 2r/s auth, `client_max_body_size 10m`) is for the **decommissioned** Container Apps path only — never runs today. Port these to the live conf. |
| High | Caddyfile absent from repo | The actual TLS edge (Caddy on the VM) is **not version-controlled** → TLS ciphers/protocols, HSTS, timeouts, body limits unauditable and drift-prone. Commit the Caddyfile. |
| High | `docker-compose.yml:63-64` (`6432:5432`), `:118-119` (`6379:6379`) | Postgres + Redis publish to host `0.0.0.0` ("remove in production" comments, but active). On the VM these are internet-reachable unless the NSG/ufw blocks them — relies on an external firewall, not config. Bind to the internal network. |
| High | repo-wide absent | **No** CAPTCHA/reCAPTCHA/hCaptcha/Turnstile on signup, login, or public verify. Only IP/velocity limits stand between a botnet and account/verify abuse. |
| Med | `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/rateLimitEnforce.ts:135-137` | App-tier limiters fail **open** on error; if Redis is down the per-client counter degrades to per-replica in-memory (inflated ceiling — [KS-170](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-170/enforceclientratelimit-runs-in-memory-per-replica-wire-the-redis)). |
| Med | `nginx-demo.conf` (no `limit_conn`/`client_body_timeout`/`client_header_timeout`) | No Slowloris/large-body/slow-request protection at the live edge. |
| Low | `nginx-demo.conf` (no active HSTS/CSP `add_header`) | Gateway emits no security headers of its own; relies wholly on downstream helmet + Caddy. Single point of omission if a service skips helmet. |

**GREEN (verified):** app-tier defence is real and layered — `express-rate-limit` global limiter (`api-gateway/src/index.ts:448`, 300/min prod), per-route login (15/15min, `:849`), register (`:861`), verification (`:469`) limiters; per-API-key distributed Redis limiter (`rateLimitEnforce.ts`); **application-level account lockout** on login (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:285-303`). Helmet provides per-service CSP + HSTS + nosniff. A standalone `observability/` module exists. The pen-tested `nginx-production.conf` is a strong hardening template — it just isn't the config in production.

**Acceptance:** WAF introduced at the edge; live gateway/Caddy config carries rate-limits/body-caps/headers; pg/redis bound internal; bot protection on public auth/verify; each with a verification test where feasible (Review G). Several items here are **new-build recommendations**, not code defects — track as remediation issues with owners.

nodes.body: Register entry: **KS-1397**, LOW (CWE-16). The nginx gateway sends `Server: nginx` on every response. The version is already hidden (`Blockchain/Dev/docker/nginx-gateway/nginx.conf:24` `server_tokens off`) and upstream `Server` is already stripped (`:142`). Akto's `UNWANTED_RESPONSE_HEADERS` flags the remaining header by name. Found by the Akto full OWASP scan on slot 4, 2026-09-30, Akto 2.36.4 (while verifying KS-1363). The decision is with Kamil: remove the header with the headers-more module, or accept it with a recorded reason.

@kamil.kreiser — a gentle follow-up on the `Server: nginx` note above, for when you have a moment. It's a small item, and the priority here stays as it is (the WAF, Postgres/Redis and CAPTCHA rows matter more). It does have one recurring cost, though, so a decision would really help.

>>> Why it's worth deciding, and the three options

**The recurring cost:** it's the only finding in the Akto security tier (slot 2, 2026-09-28, Akto 2.35.6, 50,162 results). Our gate fails on any severity, so `test:security` goes red on every run and every branch. A gate that's always red gets tuned out, and could hide the next real finding (the KS-519 shape).

**Why it has sat:** there's no config-only fix. `server_tokens off` (`nginx-demo.conf:196`) hides the version but not the name; the gateway image (`FROM nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.30-alpine`) has no `headers-more`; and the header shows on `/`, `/health/deep`, `/api/auth/login` and `/api/notifications/{id}/read`.

**Options**

1. An nginx build with `headers-more`, then `more_clear_headers Server;`.
2. Strip it at Caddy, which already terminates TLS on the VM — probably the lightest, and the same place the committed Caddyfile lives.
3. Accept it explicitly, and I'll add the test id to the Akto false-positive register so the tier reflects that decision.

Option 3 is a perfectly good answer — it's your work-stream, so it's your call. I haven't touched `nginx-demo.conf` or the gateway image. Whichever you pick, I'll wire it into the Akto harness so the tier reports honestly. Thank you.

## Small finding for this register: the gateway sends `Server: nginx` on every route (LOW)

Recording it here as the edge/WAF work-stream's home. It came up in the Akto OWASP scan during KS-1286 (Akto 2.35.6, slot 2, 2026-09-28, template `UNWANTED_RESPONSE_HEADERS`) — the only finding in a 50,162-result full run.

>>> Scope, why config alone can't remove it, and options

**Scope:** information disclosure (product fingerprinting). Akto flagged one endpoint, but the gateway sets the header, so it's every route. On slot 2:

| route | response |
|---|---|
| `PATCH /api/notifications/{id}/read` | `401`, `Server: nginx` |
| `POST /api/auth/login` | `Server: nginx` |
| `GET /health/deep` | `Server: nginx` |
| `GET /` | `Server: nginx` |

**What's already in place:** all three gateway configs set `server_tokens off` (`nginx-demo.conf:196`, `nginx-production.conf:288`, `nginx.conf:24`), which hides the version — the part that maps to CVEs. Removing the product name as well needs the `headers-more` module (`more_clear_headers Server;`), which the base image doesn't include: `Dockerfile:1` is `FROM nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.30-alpine`, `nginx -V` shows no `headers-more`, and none of the three confs uses `more_*`.

So it isn't a false positive, and there isn't a one-line config fix.

**Options, for whoever takes it**

1. An nginx build with `headers-more`, then `more_clear_headers Server;` (a non-stock base image).
2. Strip it one layer up — Caddy on the VM demo, or the ingress on the Container Apps template.
3. Accept and record it — a fingerprinting nuisance rather than an exploitable weakness.

**Effect on the scan gate:** while it stands, the full-OWASP tier FAILs by design (any severity counts), so `test:security` is red on an otherwise clean run. Worth knowing before reading that red as a regression. Cross-referenced on KS-1286.

>>>

## Re-verification against `develop` `81935f9a6` — the Caddyfile row is FALSE, and this ticket contradicts itself about it

Worked under Kam's 2026-09-02 17:34 standing instruction, and prompted by today's [KS-485 citation audit](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-485): the whole review was grounded 259 commits back, so every register row is suspect until re-checked. This ticket's banner says two rows are still live — **the strategic WAF gap** and **the absent Caddyfile**. One of those two is not live.

### 🔴 The High row "Caddyfile absent from repo" has been false since 2026-08-13

The row reads:

> **Caddyfile absent from repo** — The actual TLS edge (Caddy on the VM) is **not version-controlled** → TLS ciphers/protocols, HSTS, timeouts, body limits unauditable and drift-prone. Commit the Caddyfile.

It is at `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/caddy/Caddyfile` on `develop`, 35 lines. Added by:

```
git log --diff-filter=A -- Blockchain/Dev/deployment/caddy/Caddyfile
045c658ec  2026-08-13  KS-613/KS-615: harden the live gateway edge, keyed on the real client IP (#678)
```

Control that the search discriminates: the same sweep finds **10** versioned `nginx*.conf` files, so it is not a query that matches nothing.

The committed file does exactly what the row asked, and then some — it records the deploy path, forbids editing the VM copy in place (*"it drifts back out of version control, which is the whole finding"*), carries a **drift check** (*"committed content is byte-identical to the live `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile` as read from the VM on this date"*), and states plainly that Caddy adds no rate limiting, body cap or timeout tuning because those live one hop down in `nginx-demo.conf`.

### The contradiction is inside this ticket

The banner asserting *"Caddyfile still absent from the repo"* was added during the **session-38 closure sweep on ~2026-08-18** — **five days after** the commit that added it.

And it is the *same commit this ticket already cites approvingly*. The F-9 analysis higher up says:

> `git log -S"DELIBERATELY NOT SET HERE"` attributes it to exactly one commit — **`045c658ec`, 2026-08-13, "KS-613/KS-615: harden the live gateway edge…" (#678)** — the same hardening pass that fixed F-2, F-6 and F-7.

So the ticket cites `045c658ec` as the authority for one row while claiming, in the banner above it, that a file added *in that very commit* is still missing. The sweep that wrote the banner re-checked F-9 carefully and carried the Caddyfile row forward untested.

**This is the KS-485 rot in its most expensive form.** Not a shifted line number — a High row asserting unversioned TLS config on a live internet-facing edge, which is exactly the kind of row that gets a session allocated to it. Anyone picking this up would have gone looking for a file that has been sitting in the repo for three weeks.

### What is actually left here

**One row, and it is not ours:** the strategic Crit — *"No WAF anywhere — no ModSecurity, no Front Door/App Gateway WAF; Cloudflare is DNS-only (grey-cloud). Greenfield."* The scope note says *"Product owner explicitly wants WAF."*

That is a greenfield architecture-and-spend decision — which product, where it terminates, what it costs, who operates it. **Category 2: Kam's, not ours to start.** Bouncing rather than sizing it unasked.

**The Low row** (`nginx-demo.conf` emits no security headers of its own) was not re-verified in this pass and should be assumed to carry the same drift.

### Recommendation

Strike the Caddyfile row as **resolved at `045c658ec` (2026-08-13)** and correct the banner, which is currently the most misleading sentence on the ticket. Then KS-491 holds exactly one live item — the WAF decision — and should sit wherever this board puts things waiting on Kam, rather than reading as a three-row engineering backlog.

## Register append — F-04 is LIVE on the demo right now, and it is one symptom of a wider config finding → KS-658

**Filed 2026-08-17 (session 44).** This stream's F-04 finding ("the OpenAPI spec is a free
attack-surface map") is recorded here against the *code*. It is **live at the internet-facing edge
today**, and it was found as a control while disproving something unrelated — nobody was looking.

- `/api/docs/openapi.yaml` -> **200, text/yaml, 1,152,555 bytes** of real spec, unauthenticated
- `/api/docs/openapi.json` -> **200, application/json, 860,171 bytes**
- **Control that those 200s are evidence and not an SPA catch-all:** an invented sibling path returns
  **200 but text/html** (the Swagger UI catch-all), and `/api/health` returns a real gateway 404 JSON.

342 endpoints, every parameter and every auth mechanism. **No credentials in it** — this is a surface
map, not a secret leak, and the severity argument in KS-658 says so explicitly rather than inflating it.

**The wider finding, which is the reason it is its own ticket:** the demo runs **every** service with
`NODE_ENV=development`, while the code names `demo` as prod-like
(`services/auth/src/index.ts:220`). `ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS` is one of roughly six protections
silently inert as a result. **Three artefacts disagree** about what the demo is meant to be, so
nothing has been changed — flipping any of it would destroy the evidence that the question is open.

Full detail, measurements, the "checked and NOT true" list, and the proposed disposition: **KS-658**
(linked `related`). No change made to the VM, its `.env`, or the repo.

## Review F re-verified at `develop 2129cdc8b` — **fixed in code; whether it is fixed at the LIVE edge is NOT established**

**BLUF: every High and Med row in Review F is remediated on `develop`. The one thing that matters operationally — whether those protections are actually running on the demo VM — I could not establish read-only, and I am not asserting it in either direction.**

| Row | Code verdict at HEAD | Evidence in `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **F-2** live gateway has no rate-limit / body cap (High) | ✅ **FIXED** (KS-613, #678) | `limit_req_zone …rate=50r/s` api + `5r/s` auth (`:171-172`), `limit_conn_zone` (`:173`), `limit_req_status 429` (`:177-178`), `client_max_body_size 12m` (`:215`), applied at `:229` and `:409-410`. Counts: **9 `limit_req`, 4 `limit_conn`, 1 `client_max_body_size`** — against **0/0/0** as filed. |
| **F-3** Postgres + Redis published on `0.0.0.0` (High) | ✅ **FIXED** | `docker-compose.yml:71`, `:126`, `:167` are all **`127.0.0.1:`-bound** (`127.0.0.1:${POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT:-6432}:5432` etc.). Re-measured here independently of the Review E finding. |
| **F-6** app-tier limiter fails open (Med) | ✅ **FIXED** (KS-616, #679) | `rateLimitEnforce.ts` degrades to the in-memory ceiling **with a throttled warn** instead of silently disabling. |
| **F-7** no Slowloris / slow-request protection (Med) | ✅ **FIXED** (KS-613) | `client_body_timeout 15s` + `client_header_timeout 15s` (`:219-220`), `limit_conn secuura_conn 50` (`:224`). |
| **F-9** no security headers at the gateway (Low) | ⚠️ **PARTLY** | `X-Frame-Options: DENY` (`:251`) and `Strict-Transport-Security` (`:258`) are **active**. **CSP is still commented out** (`:595`) — so the gateway itself emits no CSP. |

### 🔴 The gap that is NOT closed, and not closeable from here
The KS-613 work is on `develop`. **A prior note on this ticket records it as not yet live on the VM, pending the Kintsugi hold.** I could not confirm or refute that read-only:

- A single read-only `GET` on the demo returns `x-frame-options: DENY`, `strict-transport-security`, and a full CSP — **but those do not discriminate.** The CSP cannot be coming from `nginx-demo.conf` (its CSP is commented out at `:595`), so it originates from a frontend's own nginx or helmet; and Caddy terminates TLS in front (`via: 1.1 Caddy`), so HSTS is not attributable either.
- The checks that *would* discriminate — tripping `limit_req` to see a 429, or exceeding `client_max_body_size` — are **abuse-shaped or write-shaped probes against a live demo**, and were not run.

**So: "F is fixed in code" is established. "F is fixed at the live edge" is UNESTABLISHED** — recorded as such rather than assumed from the merge. This is the operative question for Review F, because an edge protection that is merged but not deployed provides exactly zero protection, and the demo is internet-facing.

**Suggested disposition:** F's code rows can close; the live-edge verification should be a condition on whatever lifts the Kintsugi hold, checked with a deliberate 429 probe in a maintenance window rather than opportunistically.

### Not actioned
No code changed, nothing deployed, no rate-limit probe run against the demo.

*Verified by the Platform K session at `develop 2129cdc8b`, 2026-08-16.*

## F-4 — worse than "relies on an external firewall"

v1 hedged that the NSG/ufw might cover it. Measured on the VM today:

- `ss -lntp` → `LISTEN 0.0.0.0:6432` and `LISTEN 0.0.0.0:6379` (plus `[::]`), via docker-proxy.
- `ufw status` → **inactive**.
- `iptables -S DOCKER-USER` → **`-N DOCKER-USER` only — zero rules**.
- So **there is no host firewall of any kind**. The sole control is NSG `secuura02-demo-vmNSG`: three inbound allows (22 / 80 / 443) plus Azure's implicit `DenyAllInBound`.

Confirmed from outside: 6432 / 6379 / 5432 / 6882 filtered; 443 and 22 answer. So **nothing is exposed right now** — but it rests on one Azure rule that is not in version control, and Docker's published ports are specifically the thing that bypasses a host firewall, so anyone later "hardening the box" with ufw would get a false sense of safety.

## F-6 — the half that survived its own ticket

v1 cited [KS-170](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-170) for this finding, and **KS-170 is Done** — so F-6 reads as resolved. It is not. KS-170 fixed the per-replica counters; the **fail-open** half is still in `rateLimitEnforce.ts`:

```js
} catch (err) {
  // Rate limit check failed — allow the request (fail open)
  next();
}
```

An error in the limiter allows the request with **no limiting at all**, silently, precisely under the load that makes Redis wobble. Split out as KS-616 — otherwise it disappears with its closed parent.

## F-8 — do not close this on a live `curl`

`https://demo-pk.secuura.net/` **does** serve a full header set today: CSP, HSTS `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, nosniff, referrer-policy, permissions-policy. Anyone spot-checking would call F-8 fixed.

It is not: those come from **downstream** frontend nginx/helmet. In `nginx-demo.conf` all six security `add_header` lines are **commented out** (lines 413–420); the only live one is an `Allow` header on an internal 405 block. So the guarantee holds today and is one forgotten helmet away from not holding — exactly what v1 said.
